stem: An unknown alcohol is treated with the "Lucas reagent" to determine whether the alcohol is primary, secondary or tertiary. Which alcohol reacts fastest and by what mechanism :
solution: The Lucas reaction is mostly $\text{S}_\text{N}1$; the rate follows carbocation stability, so tertiary alcohols react fastest.

stem: Which of the following is strongest Bronsted base?
solution: Pyrrolidine has a localised $sp^3$ lone pair on N, so it is protonated most easily.
notes: Options are structures in the source; transcribed as names.

stem: Calamine, malachite, magnetite and cryolite, respectively are:
The naturally occurring amino acid that contains only one basic functional group in its chemical structure is
solution: Asparagine has only one basic group; the others are basic amino acids with more than one.

stem: Which of the following substances show the highest colligative properties?

stem: Which of the following complexes will exhibit maximum attraction to an applied magnetic field?
solution: Unpaired electrons: Zn$^{2+}$ ($d^{10}$) 0; Co$^{2+}$ ($d^7$, high spin) 3; Co$^{3+}$ with en ($d^6$, low spin) 0; Ni$^{2+}$ ($d^8$) 2.
